about: Vietti is one of the great names of Barolo, based in the hilltop village of Castiglione Falletto in the heart of the Langhe. The family farmed and made wine here in the nineteenth century, and Mario Vietti began bottling under the family name in 1919. After Alfredo Currado married Luciana Vietti and took over in 1960, the house became a pioneer of single-vineyard Barolo and helped rescue the near-forgotten white grape Arneis. Since 2016 the estate has been owned by the American Krause family, who kept its vineyards and team intact.

Trevìe, long sold as “Tre Vigne” (three vineyards), is Vietti’s classic Barbera d’Alba, drawn from old vines of 28 to 43 years in Castiglione Falletto, Monforte d’Alba and neighbouring Langhe villages, on calcareous clay soils. The grapes are hand-harvested and fermented in stainless steel, then the wine finishes malolactic fermentation and ages roughly fourteen months in oak, a mix of barriques and larger casks, before bottling.

The winery describes ruby colour, ripe red cherry and vanilla on the nose, and a palate of bright acidity and sweet tannins with the oak well folded in. Antonio Galloni of Vinous called the 2022 a superb wine, noting dark cherry, plum and mocha carried by real freshness, the hallmark of Barbera’s naturally high acidity.
facts: Old vines (28–43 years) in Castiglione Falletto, Monforte d’Alba and other Langhe villages
Fermented in stainless steel; malolactic in barrel
About 14 months in oak (barriques and larger casks)
